findings.description: The verified root docs compile test (OPS-HTTP-004, `src/test/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/docs/DocsExamplesCompileTest.java:502`) fails when a skipped block compiles ("these skipped blocks compile now; drop their skip entries"). SKIPS holds `websocket.md` (2 x "later-wave method `RestApp.ws`"), `lifecycle.md` ("RestApp app = RestApp.create();", "later-wave method `RestApp.ws`") and `json.md` ("later-wave method `WebSocketSession.sendJson`"). Once wave 7 adds `ws`, those blocks compile (or their reason becomes untrue) and the verified test breaks. Only OPS-SSE-001 AC-4 removes its own (sse.md) skips; no wave-7 AC owns the websocket.md, lifecycle.md and json.md entries. OPS-WS-001 AC-6 instead names a different mechanism ("compiled by a test source that copies it (the wave 6 docs-test pattern)") that does not exist: WaveSixDocsTest compiles nothing, and OPS-WS-001's trace points at WaveSixDocsTest.java.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite OPS-WS-001 AC-6: "Every Java code block of `docs/api/websocket.md` is compiled by the root docs compile test of OPS-HTTP-004 with no skip entry naming `websocket.md` except app-defined-type reasons (the `Auth` block), the `lifecycle.md` skip whose reason is `later-wave method RestApp.ws` is removed, the `json.md` skip reason no longer names `WebSocketSession.sendJson` as a later-wave method, and a `WAVE_SEVEN_MEMBERS` check (ws, webSocket, sse, sendJson, onJson, SseEvent ...) finds no skip naming a wave 7 member as later-wave; `./gradlew build` passes." Change the trace from WaveSixDocsTest.java to DocsExamplesCompileTest.java.

findings.description: "With `idleTimeout(1, SECONDS)` and `pingInterval(30, SECONDS)`, a session ... is handed close `1001` within 2 s by the scheduler, even while its client answers Pings". With a 30 s ping interval TinyHttpd sends no Ping inside the 2 s window, so the clause that proves D-425's reason (TinyHttpd counts Ping/Pong as activity) cannot occur; the AC is untestable as written and D-425 is only nominally covered on that point.
findings.suggested_fix: "With `idleTimeout(1, SECONDS)` and `pingInterval(30, SECONDS)`, a session whose client sends a Ping frame every 300 ms but no text or binary message is handed close `1001` by the scheduler within 2 s of its last text or binary message, the client receives a Pong for each Ping until then, and `onClose` receives `1001` (T21). [D-425; D-323]"

findings.ac: FR-WS-007 AC-6; FR-WS-010 AC-2; FR-WS-008 AC-4; FR-WS-005 AC-8; FR-APP-019 AC-9
findings.description: Several ACs assert the close code/reason delivered to `onClose` and the access-log close line for server-initiated closes ("`onClose` receives `1008`" with a non-reading client, "onClose listeners run once with `1001`", "`onClose` receives `(4000, \"bye\")`"). TinyHttpd 46b973e `WebSocket.run` reports to `WebSocketListener.onClose` the code/reason of the peer's close frame; when the server sent close and the peer does not answer before the read timeout, or the socket is aborted, it reports `1006` (closeCode stays ABNORMAL), and the reason is whatever the peer echoed (often empty). A stalled client in FR-WS-007 AC-6 never answers, so `onClose` would receive 1006, not 1008. No requirement states the core rule that makes these ACs achievable.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a decision AC to FR-WS-006: "When the server initiated the close (`ws.close`, overflow, idle timeout, shutdown, listener exception) with code c and reason r, `onClose` and the FR-APP-019 close line report (c, r) whatever the peer answers or whether the socket was aborted; otherwise they report the code and reason TinyHttpd delivers, and `1006` with an empty reason for an abort without a close frame. Decision: the server's own close code wins." Re-tag FR-WS-005 AC-8, FR-WS-007 AC-6, FR-WS-008 AC-4, FR-WS-010 AC-2/AC-7 and FR-APP-019 AC-9 to it.

findings.description: Verified FR-HTTP-022 AC-6 (not superseded) is evidenced by `HttpAcceptanceTest#sdsAc18_T06_FR_HTTP_022_AC5_AC6_webSocketOnlyHookRouteGives426`, which sends `Upgrade: websocket` + `Connection: Upgrade` to the `TestApp.webSocketRoute` hook and expects `426`. FR-WS-001 AC-7 makes such requests reach `HttpExchange.webSocket`, and IR-WS-001 rationale makes the hook "the implementation of `ws`" (the hook and the `TestApp.webSocketRoute(path)` fixture take a `RouteHandler` today and are used by StaticMethodTest, MiddlewarePipelineTest, ErrorPathTest, DefaultRestAppTest). The rationale only says "tests asserting that 426 are re-pointed here"; no AC names the replaced test, the fixture's fate or the FR-HTTP-022 AC-6 evidence update.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to FR-WS-001 AC-7: "`HttpAcceptanceTest#sdsAc18_...AC6...` keeps its non-upgrade `426` case and its upgrade case is replaced by this AC's test; the `TestApp.webSocketRoute(path)` fixture and the internal hook either keep their `RouteHandler` signature or are re-pointed to `ws` with every caller (StaticMethodTest FR-STATIC-002 AC-4, MiddlewarePipelineTest, ErrorPathTest, DefaultRestAppTest) still passing", and add a Change Note on FR-HTTP-022 that AC-6 is historical from wave 7.

findings.description: Decision accepts close codes "1000..4999 excluding 1004, 1005, 1006 and 1015", which admits 1016..2999 (unassigned/IANA-reserved). TinyHttpd's own `sendableCloseCode` (RFC 6455 7.4) accepts only 1000-1003, 1007-1014 and 3000-4999 and fails a received close with such a code as a protocol error, so a NaruServe server sending close(2000) to a TinyHttpd-like or Autobahn-strict client gets the connection failed. The rationale claims this range is "per RFC 6455 section 7.4".
findings.suggested_fix: "`close(1005, \"\")`, `close(999, \"\")`, `close(2000, \"\")` and `close(5000, \"\")` throw `IllegalArgumentException`, ...; `close(1012, \"\")`, `close(3000, \"\")` and `close(4999, \"x\")` are accepted. Decision: the close code must be 1000-1003, 1007-1014 or 3000-4999 (the sendable set of TinyHttpd's `WebSocket`), and the reason must fit 123 UTF-8 bytes."

findings.description: "... and no value means unlimited" reads as "leaving a setting unset means unlimited", which contradicts the defaults of IR-WS-001 AC-7 / IR-SSE-001 AC-5. The rationale ("no value means unlimited") has the same ambiguity; the intent is I-012 (no accepted value is unlimited).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with "and no accepted value of any setting means unlimited (I-012)."

findings.description: AC-2 defines `send` as returning "`true` when the event was written or queued and `false` when the client has already ended", but FR-SSE-002 AC-4 makes the overflowing send return `false` on a client that had not yet ended (it ends because of that send). The two definitions disagree on the overflow case.
findings.suggested_fix: "... `send` returns `true` when the event was written or queued, and `false` when it was not (the client had already ended, or the send overflowed the queue and ended the stream as FR-SSE-002 states)."

findings.description: Disconnect detection is bounded to "one heartbeat interval plus 1 s". After the peer closes, the first write to the socket usually succeeds (it only elicits a RST) and only the next write fails, so detection can take up to two heartbeat intervals; with a 1 s heartbeat the 2 s bound is flaky.
findings.suggested_fix: Use "within two heartbeat intervals plus 1 s (with `heartbeatInterval` 1 s: 3 s)" in both ACs and in the FR-SSE-004 rationale pitfall.

findings.description: The requirement says "event-stream and upgrade paths ... run the TinyHttpd WebSocket handshake" and AC-2 bans any `UnsupportedOperationException` naming wave 7 in TinyHttpdFeatures, but the wave decision keeps the raw `upgrade(headers, UpgradeHandler)` "for raw upgrades" and no AC states what the raw upgrade does on TinyHttpd at wave 7 (implemented through `Response.upgrade`, or still unsupported with a non-wave message). The raw upgrade and `webSocket` are conflated.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to AC-2: "The raw `upgrade(headers, UpgradeHandler)` path on TinyHttpd <either: writes 101 through `Response.upgrade(protocol)` and calls the handler with the `UpgradedConnection` streams / or: throws `UnsupportedOperationException` stating that raw upgrades are not supported by the TinyHttpd adapter in v1>, which a test asserts. Decision: ..."; keep the requirement text distinguishing `webSocket` from the raw `upgrade`.

findings.description: "a docs test of the wave close finds that entry in the release test results file" names no file path or entry phrase, so the AC cannot be checked deterministically.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the file and phrase, e.g. "... in `docs/research/naruserve-v1/waves/wave-7/release-test-results.md` under the heading `Manual follow-up: low-end Android tuning`, which a docs test finds".

findings.description: `docs/api/defaults.md:26` reads `| WebSocket 송신 큐(연결당) | 1 MiB | — | 예외 또는 연결 종료 | **(미확정)** |`. findings.description: A single message larger than `sendQueueSize` (e.g. 1.5 MiB with the 1 MiB default) closes a healthy idle session with 1008; the AC does not state this edge, which an Express/ws user would not expect.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: "a single message larger than `sendQueueSize` overflows on an empty queue and closes with 1008 the same way" (or decide otherwise) and record it in websocket.md.

findings.suggested_fix: Add to AC-5: "and a stalled session's sender thread is released once TinyHttpd's `writeTimeout` (set to 1 s in the test) aborts its socket".

findings.description: D-313 "stored per connection in a concurrent map" is only tagged; AC-2 does not assert concurrent access.

findings.description: The request mark is a ThreadLocal (`AppLifecycle.enterRequest`); the in-memory adapter runs the drain on its own worker thread (IR-HTTP-007 AC-3), so the mark must be set on that thread too. AC-8 names no adapter.
findings.suggested_fix: State "over the in-memory adapter and over TinyHttpd" and that the drain thread enters the request mark before the drain loop.

findings.description: The `cause` for an SSE stream force-closed by the adapter stop at the deadline (FR-SSE-005 AC-5) and the close code logged for a session aborted without a close frame (FR-WS-010 AC-7) are not defined.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: force-closed stream -> `cause=shutdown`; aborted session -> close code `1006` (or the server's own code per the close-code decision).
